Stick
stĭk
n. (a piece of wood; rendering Hebrew ets, Greek phruganon)
Old English sticca. A stick is the plainest object in Scripture, and it is repeatedly the material of a sign.

Biblical Definition

A stick is a piece of wood. Ezekiel is told to take two and join them: “join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand” (Eze 37:17), a sign of Judah and Israel reunited. The widow of Zarephath is gathering two sticks to cook a last meal (1Ki 17:10). Paul gathers a bundle of sticks on Malta and is bitten by a viper out of the heat (Act 28:3), and a man is stoned for gathering them on the sabbath (Num 15:32).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines stick as the small shoot or branch of a tree or shrub, cut off; a rod; and a staff.

expand to see more

STICK, n. The small shoot or branch of a tree or shrub, cut off; a rod; also, a staff.

2. Any stem of a plant of a size to be cut for fuel.

Key Scripture

Eze 37:17 — "And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand."

1Ki 17:10 — "So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink."

Act 28:3 — "And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand."

Num 15:32 — "And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man that gathered sticks upon the sabbath day."

Modern Corruption

Unity is pursued by argument and negotiation, and Ezekiel's sign shows two sticks becoming one in the prophet's hand — the joining done by someone other than the sticks.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 37's second sign follows the valley of dry bones and belongs with it. Two sticks, one for Judah and one for Joseph, are written on and then joined so that they become one in thine hand. The prophet does the joining; the sticks contribute nothing but their separateness. Set beside the bones that could not assemble themselves, the message is consistent — both resurrection and reunion are acts of God, and the people involved are told to prophesy rather than to organize.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ets (H6086), wood or tree — the same word for a living tree and a cut stick; Greek phruganon (G5434), dry sticks or brushwood.

expand to see more

Hebrew ets (H6086) — tree, wood, stick; Ezekiel 37:16-20, 1 Kings 17:10.

Greek phruganon (G5434) — dry sticks, brushwood; only Acts 28:3, Paul's bundle on Malta.

Usage

"“They shall become one in thine hand” — the joining is not the sticks' work."

"“Gathering of two sticks” — the widow's last meal."

"“Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks” — the apostle doing the fire duty."
